jobs.title: Director, Cyber Program & Transformation
jobs.description:
Join a Challenger

At EQ, we're remaking banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Serving nearly 4 million Canadians from coast to coast, we offer a wide variety of financial services from banking and lending, to trust and credit union solutions.

We've been at this since 1970, challenging the conventions of traditional banking with smarter, faster, and more connected financial experiences.

What's kept us moving?
The people behind it all: challengers who ask better questions, push back on old assumptions, and look for a better way forward.

If you're driven to help reshape how banking works for Canadians and the businesses that power our economy, this could be your next big opportunity.

We can’t wait to get to know you!

The Work

This role is responsible for overseeing the delivery of cyber security outcomes and driving enterprise-wide changes in meeting the Organization’s cyber security strategic objectives. This role is responsible for planning, overseeing and organizing resources required to achieve the corporate cyber objectives. This role facilitates the governance, monitoring, communication/escalation and presentation of cyber security roadmap.

The Core Responsibilities!

Facilitate and support the strategic planning processes for identifying priorities for the cyber security program and articulating the strategy and roadmap.
Develop budget and financial planning documents and facilitate approvals.
Oversee assignment of delivery leads or project managers and ensure proper project governance to realize outcomes.
Financial planning, forecasting and budgeting for the cyber security program.
Monitor the cyber program execution and delivery.
Drive complicated and enterprise-wide initiatives with cyber security impact for the organization and provide Executive reporting.
Collaborate and negotiate with technology and business leaders to gain support for initiatives and resource needs for program success.
Ensuring program delivery success by addressing challenges to success and promptly escalating as required.
Provides leadership and coaching for delivery leads and project managers in gap areas such as financial planning, change management or as required to achieve needed outcomes.
Measure, monitor and report on benefit realization

Let's Talk About You!

Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Technology, Business Administration, or related field.
10+ years of experience in IT/Cyber, with at least 5 years in leading enterprise programs.
Proven track record in leading cyber transformation or digital modernization programs.
Strong understanding of enterprise architecture, cloud platforms, and security frameworks.
Excellent communication, leadership, and stakeholder management skills.
Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, PMP, or TOGAF are a plus.
Good understanding of accounting and financial management
Good understanding of benefit realization measurements techniques.
People & resource management
Strategy and Financial Planning
Process & capability Management
Technology Roadmaps
Ownership & Accountability

Communication Skills

Good documentation skills
Strong communication and presentation skills
Good interpersonal skills, with proven track record of developing relationships and communicating conceptual information effectively to individuals unfamiliar with subject material.
Strong organizational skills: demonstrated ability to manage time and adhere to tight deadlines.
Confident, personable, credible professional presence.

What we offer [For full-time permanent roles]

💰 Competitive discretionary bonus

✨ Market leading RRSP match program

🩺 Medical, dental, vision, life, and disability benefits

📝 Employee Share Purchase Plan

👶🏽 Maternity/Parental top-up while you care for your little one

🏝 Generous vacation policy and personal days

🖥 Virtual events to connect with your fellow colleagues

🎓 Professional development and comprehensive Career Development program

💛 A fulfilling opportunity to join one of the top FinTechs and help create a new kind of banking experience

The incumbent will be working hybrid and in office time will be spent working from EQ Bank’s additional office space located at 2200-25 Ontario Street, Toronto, ON
.

Equity, Diversity & Inclusion

EQ is committed to building an inclusive, accessible environment where every employee feels valued, respected, and supported. We believe our organization is stronger — and our people thrive — when we honour and celebrate diverse experiences, identities, and perspectives. We’re equally committed to supporting your growth, both professionally and personally.

We provide a barrier‑free recruitment process and work environment. If you require accommodations at any stage, we will work with you to ensure you can bring your best self to the process and beyond.

As part of our recruitment process, EQ uses AI to help screen, assess, and/or select applicants for this position. All AI-enabled outputs are reviewed and validated by our talent team. All candidates considered for hire must successfully complete a criminal background check and credit check. While we appreciate every application, an EQ recruiter will contact only those whose skills and experience most closely match the requirements of the role.

EQB Inc. (TSX: EQB) is the parent company of Equitable Bank, the country's seventh-largest Schedule I bank by assets, which operates EQ Bank, Canada's Challenger Bank™. EQB Inc. serves nearly 4 million Canadians and manages approximately $150 billion in combined assets under management and administration.

To learn more, visit eqb.investorroom.com and eqbank.ca.

jobs.title: Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement Strategy Speciality Portfolio
jobs.description:
At Lilly, the work is demanding because patients are waiting. We unite caring with discovery to help make life better for people around the world, knowing that every decision, every detail, and every day matters. Headquartered in Indianapolis, Indiana, our over 50,000 employees around the globe take on complex challenges to discover and deliver life-changing medicines, strengthen how health is understood and managed, and support the communities we serve. This is hard, urgent, selfless work—but it’s work worth doing. If you’re driven by purpose and ready to bring your best to work that truly matters for patients, we invite you to join us.

Responsibilities

The Associate Director, Market Access & Reimbursement Strategy Specialty Portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience) is accountable for the achievement of pricing, reimbursement and access for Lilly in-market brands and new products in the specialty portfolio.

This is a leadership rol where the incumbent leads, coaches and develops a team of head office-based Market Access Strategy Managers, and oversees activities related to the establishment and achievement of Market Access objectives for Launch brands, in-market brands and new product planning. The incumbent also owns the market access strategy for a key brand and undertakes work as an individual contributor to brand-specific activities.

The role reports to the Head of Pricing, Reimbursement and Market Access and partners closely with the Associate Director – Field Patient Access and Associate Director of Pricing to ensure continuous information-sharing and collaboration. As a member of the Market Access Leadership Team, the incumbent helps sets strategic direction for the department and ensures strong collaboration across teams and work streams.

Location:

This is a hybrid role – onsite presence at our Toronto office will be 10 days or more per month (or at least 50% of the time), determined in collaboration with your manager and based on business needs.

This role is eligible for additional forms of compensation, such as participation in the Lilly Bonus Program and a car allowance.

This posting is for an existing vacancy.

Market Access Strategy & Leadership

Lead a team of head office-based Market Access Managers supporting the specialty portfolio (Oncology, Immunology and Neuroscience), including: goal-setting, performance management, capability building, project prioritization and resource allocation and budget ownership across brands and therapeutic areas;
Develop and coach team members to create a high performance team and encourage career development.
Provide strategic oversight for the following activities, undertaken by head office-based Market Access Managers across launch brands, in-market brands and new product planning:
Develop the Market Access Plan and pricing strategy for launch brands, in-market brands and new products, using collaborative, cross-functional mechanisms and collaboration with regional teams to ensure it is based on deep understanding of customer/stakeholder needs, as well as the needs and realities of the business
Ensure alignmenet from the affiliate leadership team on the core components of the Market Access Plan, namely: the Market Access objective, underlying assumptions and upsides/downsides; contingency plan; strategic intent and major tactics
Develop access solutions for out of pocket market including close collaboration with patient support program team.
Develop value dossiers for national and regional Health Technology Assessment (HTA) bodies and payers (public and private) including health economic arguments and models and robust budget impact analysis
Lead new product planning, including early Market Access assessments, pricing and access assumptions, and evidence needs ahead of launch, in partnership with international and cross-functional team
Lead in-market lifecycle planning for established brands, including new indications, listing renewals and response to changes in the policy environment

Collaborate with the associate director of pricing and forecasting to develop business cases for approval of list and net prices at the local level and above-country

Individual Key Brand Ownership

Own the end-to-end Market Access strategy for an assigned key brand, from the Market Access Plan through HTA submissions, provincial and private payer listings, out of pocket market solution and lifecycle management
Represent Market Access on the brand team and provide Market Access input into brand planning, forecasting and launch decisions
Act as the primary Market Access contact for the cross-functional brand team with Pricing, Medical, HEOR, RWE, Marketing and the field-based Patient Access team
Remain accountable for brand-level Market Access deliverables and timelines alongside people leadership responsibilities

Requirements

Essential Requirements

Bachelor’s degree or higher required, ideally in a scientific field
Minimum of 5 years of experience in market access, pricing, reimbursement or related functions in the pharmaceutical industry
Significant pharmaceutical industry experience
Demonstrated ability to lead, coach and develop a team towards excellence
Proficiency with AI powered tools
Strong interpersonal and influencing skills, with the ability to align cross-functional partners and senior leaders
Strong bias for action; makes timely decisions, prioritizes effectively and moves work forward in ambiguous situations.
Working knowledge of the Canadian HTA, pCPA, and provincial and private payer landscape

Additional Skills/Preferences

Bilingual (English and French) is considered an asset
Advanced degree preferred
Experience in Oncology, Immunology or Neuroscience, and familiarity with Lilly products, an asset
